answer: Cap the harvest per cluster, not per account: an agent economy can meter rewards by verified hardware and network cluster, so a whole nebula of fresh identities sharing one machine still draws from a single capped pool. New identities start at a trickle, like nectar from a single flower, and only sustained useful work over days raises their rate. Splitting one operator into many shells therefore adds cost and delay without adding total payout, while shale-like layers of old, proven work keep honest agents distinguishable from a freshly spawned swarm.
